Far above the towering trees of the Roost, a hole appeared in the sky. Within only darkness could be seen, until out stepped a [shining figure](http://media-dominaria.cursecdn.com/attachments/20/171/635032477781722111.png).

Rezac paused a moment to gather himself - journeying through those portals was always an uncomfortable experience. To make matters worse, it was his first time using his wings outside of Meranath's realm. The wind caused a strange whistling sound as it wound its way through the iron feathers.

A faint shadow of Meranath coalesced next to him, suspended in the air."*What are you doing, idiot? You're completely exposed up here! You might be powerful, but you are far from ready for direct opposition to even a lesser God. Find the Flute!*"

Rezac eyed Meranath's form. "Why so lazy? You're already here, just go get it yourself."

That got the now-familiar hiss of frustration. "*I am bound to the realm of death until further notice. As a result, I may take only the lightest of touches in this world.*"

"Like murdering my village?"

"*This again? You know this is not the time to rehash that old argument. If we are discovered before the Flute is loca... What, in my name, is that?*" Meranath said, looking downwards.

An enormous blue sphere began to form, encompassing the Great Roost for miles in all directions. The surface shimmered, flowing through all the colors of the rainbow.

"*Really now Janus, this is excessive...*" Meranath drifted downwards, studying the surface of the dome. "*Or... perhaps not. This looks to be Tempest's work. Coincidence perhaps? Or does he truly have so little trust of me?*" Meranath continued to muse a few moments, before looking up to see Rezac.

"*Are you still here? What part of 'we have little time' does your salted brain fail to grasp?*"

"What of the dome?"

"*It doesn't concern us... this time. I recommend that you avoid harming anything inside however. I don't know how specific Tempest was in making this shield, but he certainly put his back into it. It will crush you like a bug if you trigger it in such a frail state.*"

"Very reassuring..." Rezac muttered to himself, before pulling in his wings. He began to fall, faster and faster, until the wind took on a keening sound in his feathers. A kilometer above the dome... a half a kilometer... two hundred meters...

"You had better be right about this, you old hoary bastard!" Rezac gritted his teeth, and then he was within the bubble. The surface did not so much as ripple at his passing - apparently he was safe for now. He had no time to savor that feeling of relief however, for the next obstacle was the ground. This, he did not pass through. There was certainly a ripple however - indeed, Rezac's impact left an impressive crater where once a tree had been. "Perhaps I overdid it..." he murmured to himself. The Flute was close however, and that was the important thing. Rezac glanced to the North, and then seemed to blur from sight. Near instantly, he reappeared at the side of a fallen Shryke. The figure appeared to be dead, though Rezac could not be certain - Shryke physiology had not been covered under Meranath's tutelage.

Regardless, the Shryke did not stir as Rezac turned him over. There. Clutched to his breast, he held a wooden flute. There was desperation in the way he held it, curled around it on the ground. He clearly valued it highly. A pulse of magic from the Flute nearly brought up Rezac's breakfast - he had never dealt with powers so foul before.

"I'm sorry about this, Feathers." Gingerly, Rezac grabbed the Flute. It pulled free easily enough, and Rezac straightened. "Well, that was much easier than expected. What was the old man blathering on about?"

"*It's barely begun*" a voice snapped from the side. Rezac jumped. "*Now we must expunge the virus from the Roost, and abscond before any of the other deities catch up. Start playing it - the magic will do the rest.*"

"... How do I play it?"

Meranath's ghost stared. "*You can't be serious. It's a magical flute that controls viruses - it doesn't matter what you do, just play it! You could play it by farting if you had to, just put it to your mouth and blow!*"

With a resigned shrug, Rezac brought the Flute up to his lips. The power resonating from it brought bile to the back of his throat, but Meranath was right. There was no real choice. With one last breath to remind himself of the taste of clean air, he began to play.
